questions.question: 1. Which one of the following is an example of an unsorted array?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This array is sorted in ascending order.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This array is sorted in ascending order.
explanations.c: Correct. This array is unsorted as elements are not in any particular order (neither ascending nor descending).
explanations.d: Incorrect. This array is sorted in descending order.

questions.question: 2. Suppose an algorithm goes through each element of an array twice. What is the time complexity of the algorithm? (N: the size of the array)

explanations.a: Correct. Going through each element twice means 2*N operations, which simplifies to O(N) in asymptotic notation as constant factors are dropped.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(N^2) would mean nested iterations through the array.
explanations.c: Incorrect. O(NlogN) is typical for efficient sorting algorithms like merge sort.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(N^0.5) would mean sublinear time, which does not match traversing all elements twice.

questions.question: 3. Which of the following is false about the array?

answers.a: O(N) insertion at a random index
answers.c: O(1) deletion of a random element

explanations.a: Incorrect. O(N) insertion at a random index is true as elements may need to be shifted.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(1) lookup is true for arrays as we can directly access elements by index.
explanations.c: Correct. This is false because deletion of a random element in an array requires O(N) time, not O(1), as elements need to be shifted to fill the gap.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(N) search in unsorted array is true as we may need to check every element.

questions.question: 4. Sorting an array makes searching faster.

explanations.a: Correct. Sorting an array enables efficient search algorithms like binary search with O(log N) complexity, compared to O(N) for linear search in unsorted arrays.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Sorting an array does make searching faster by enabling more efficient search algorithms.

questions.question: 5. What is the time complexity of the following algorithm? for i = 0; i < n; i++ for j = i+1; j < n; j++ for k = j+1; k < n; k++ printf(array[(i+j+k)%n])

explanations.a: Incorrect. O(N) would be for a single loop.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(N^2) would be for two nested loops.
explanations.c: Correct. Three nested loops each running up to N gives O(N^3) time complexity.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(N^0.5) is not the correct complexity for nested loops.
